content_pages.title: Getting started
content_pages.post_content:
Getting started

We're really looking forward to getting started on this project — and we hope you are, too. This guide gives you everything you need to get the most out of working together.

Here's what we'll cover:

  • How the process works
  • What you can expect in terms of deliverables and timelines
  • Your crucial role in the project
  • Who's working on your project and how to reach us

Have a read through in your own time. If anything is left unanswered, your main point of contact is your project lead — details are in the Useful links section at the end.

What to expect from working together

We do things a little differently. Instead of just asking for your requirements, going away, and producing set deliverables, we work with you to create something that will have a real impact on your business.

  • Experience-driven approach — everything we do is based on years of applying the same tactics to our own work
  • Truly collaborative — your input is key to the success of the project. We work around you, taking into account any guidelines you need us to follow
  • Senior team, start to finish — we do the work ourselves. We're not salespeople who throw projects over the wall to juniors
  • No cookie-cutter solutions — every project is unique and we treat it that way

Setup note: introduce your portal

A short walkthrough video here — how to navigate the portal, find deliverables, and leave feedback — saves a surprising number of emails. Record a two-minute screen capture with Loom or similar and embed it in this spot. Delete this note before sharing.

Your role in the project

A lot of clients think they should stay out of the way and let us do our thing. But you have a much bigger role in the success of a project than you might think. Here's how to get the most out of working together.

Be the expert on your business

No matter how good we are, you will always know more about your business than we do. We research thoroughly before each project, but your experience is more valuable than most of what we can dig up.

Don't be afraid to give context on everything, even if you think it isn't relevant. The more we know, the better equipped we are to build something tailor-made for you.

Manage your team and decision-makers

It's your job to get your team in order and decide who is responsible for what. It's best to set roles at the very start of the project and state clearly who signs things off.

If that person is you, you need to be involved throughout. Dropping in periodically makes it hard to know what's going on and to make informed decisions.

Give feedback in good time

We pride ourselves on producing great work in a reasonable timeframe, and that depends on hearing back from you. Late feedback has a knock-on effect on every stage that follows.

If anything is unclear at any point, the Ask us anything section is the fastest way to get an answer.

Keep everything in one place

This portal is the single source of truth for the project. Files, feedback, and decisions all live here, so nothing gets lost in an email thread or a chat message from three weeks ago.

Who you'll be working with

Setup note: introduce the team

Add a short profile for each person on the project — name, role, and one line on what they're responsible for. A photo each makes it friendlier, and a three-column layout works well. Clients are far more likely to reach out to a name and a face than to an inbox. Delete this note before sharing.

How the project runs

Every project moves through the same three stages. You can see which one we're in at any time from the phases on the portal home page.

What happens next

Your first three steps

  1. Fill in the design questionnaire so we understand where you're heading
  2. Upload your brand assets — logos, fonts, and anything else we should work with
  3. Book your kickoff call using the link in the Kickoff meeting module

That's everything

Work through the modules on the home page in your own time. Anything marked with a due date needs your attention first — everything else is here for reference whenever you need it.

content_pages.title: Design questionnaire
content_pages.post_content:
Design questionnaire

This questionnaire helps us understand your preferences, goals, and vision for the new site. Take your time with each question — the more detail you give us, the better we can tailor the design to what you actually need.

There are no wrong answers. We want to understand how you see your brand and what matters most to you and your audience.

Setup note: add your form

Use your preferred form tool (Gravity Forms, Typeform, Google Forms, or whatever you already own) to build a form from the questions below, then paste the embed code or shortcode here. Once your form is in place you can delete the question list. Delete this note before sharing.

⚡️ Quick tip

When you ask for reference sites, always ask why — not just which ones. A client who sends five links has given you a mood board; a client who says "I like how this one explains pricing without a table" has given you a brief. The single most useful question in this whole list is the follow-up: what specifically appeals to you about it?

Brand and identity

  • How would you describe your brand personality in three to five words? (for example: professional, innovative, friendly, bold, trustworthy)
  • What do you want visitors to feel when they land on your site?
  • Do you have existing brand guidelines? If so, please upload them in the Brand assets module.
  • Are there any brand elements that must stay exactly as they are? (a logo, a colour, a tagline)
  • What sets you apart from your competitors?

Your audience

  • Who is your primary audience? Describe who they are, what they care about, and what they need.
  • What is the main action you want visitors to take? (get in touch, buy something, sign up)
  • How do most people find your site at the moment? (search, social, referrals, word of mouth)
  • What devices do they mostly use?

Competitors and inspiration

  • List three to five competitor websites. What do you like or dislike about each?
  • Share three to five sites you admire — they don't need to be in your industry. What specifically appeals to you about each one?
  • Are there design styles you're drawn to? (minimalism, bold typography, illustration, dark mode)
  • Are there any you want us to avoid?

Features and functionality

  • What does the new site need to do? (contact forms, booking, blog, shop, portfolio)
  • Does it need to connect to anything you already use? (CRM, email marketing, payments, analytics)
  • Who will be updating the site day to day, and how comfortable are they doing it?
  • Are there accessibility requirements we should design to?
  • Do you have specific SEO goals?

Content

  • What pages do you think the new site needs?
  • Is there existing content you want to bring across?
  • Will you need help with the writing?
  • Do you have photography we can use, or should we plan for stock?

When we need this by: please try to get your answers back within five working days. If you need longer, just say — your answers shape the whole design direction, so a thorough response matters more than a fast one.

content_pages.title: Ask us anything
content_pages.post_content:
Ask us anything

Not sure about something? Ask here rather than saving it up. There's a comment thread at the bottom of this page — post a question and we'll answer it there, so the whole conversation stays in one place instead of scattered across email.

No question is too small. If something about the process, the timeline, or a decision we've made isn't clear, it's worth asking.

Setup note: turn comments on

This page is built around a comment thread, and there are two switches to check before it appears. First, turn comments on for your portals — how to enable comments in your portals. Then open this page in the editor and make sure Discussion → Allow comments is ticked, since an imported page picks that up from your site's default rather than from the template. Delete this note before sharing.

Getting a useful answer

A couple of things that help us give you a straight answer first time:

  • Say what you're looking at — which page, section, or file, so we're both talking about the same thing
  • Say what you're trying to do — the goal behind the question often changes the answer
  • Tell us if it's blocking you — we'll jump the queue for anything holding up your side of the work

⚡️ Quick tip

Questions get better results than requests. Instead of asking for a specific change, try asking why something was done a certain way. A request narrows things to one option; a question opens up the reasoning, and the answer is often a better fix than either of us had in mind. We spend a lot of time deliberating behind the scenes and we'd far rather talk it through than silently make the change.

When you'll hear back

We check this thread every working day and usually reply the same day. If something is urgent, say so in your comment and we'll prioritise it.

Setup note: set your own response time

Change the line above to whatever you can actually commit to. A response time you hit every time is worth more than a fast one you miss. Delete this note before sharing.

content_pages.title: Site management guide
content_pages.post_content:
Managing your new website

Congratulations on your new website. This guide covers what you need to know to keep it updated, secure, and running smoothly.

You've got this

WordPress is designed to be straightforward. Most day-to-day tasks — editing text, adding images, publishing posts — are about as hard as using a word processor. If you get stuck, come back to this guide.

Updating content

  • Blog posts: go to Posts → Add New
  • Pages: go to Pages and click any page to edit
  • Images: use the Media Library to upload and manage images
  • Menus: go to Appearance → Menus to update navigation

Keeping the site updated

WordPress, themes, and plugins release regular updates for security and new features. Here's how to stay current.

Always back up first

Before running any updates, make sure you have a recent backup. Your host may take them automatically, or you can use a plugin like UpdraftPlus.

To check for updates, go to Dashboard → Updates. You'll see everything available for WordPress core, plugins, and themes. Select what you want and click update.

A note on plugin updates

Some premium plugins need a valid licence key to receive updates. If an update fails, check the licence hasn't expired before assuming anything is broken.

Security basics

Do

  • Keep WordPress and plugins updated
  • Use strong, unique passwords
  • Run regular backups
  • Keep an eye on login attempts

Don't

  • Install plugins or themes from untrusted sources
  • Share admin credentials by email
  • Ignore update notifications
  • Delete files from the server directly

Never edit core files

Anything in wp-includes/ or wp-admin/ should never be edited directly. Your changes will be wiped by the next update, and you risk opening a security hole in the meantime.

Getting help

Setup note: add your support details

Replace the list below with how you actually want clients to reach you after launch, and be specific about response times — this is the section people read when something has gone wrong. Delete this note before sharing.

  1. Check this guide first — most common questions are answered here
  2. Email us for anything non-urgent and we'll come back to you within one working day
  3. For anything urgent — the site is down, or something is broken in public — call us

content_pages.title: What happens next
content_pages.post_content:
What happens next

Your site is live. Here's what that means day to day, and what we can keep doing for you if you'd like us to.

The first two weeks

We keep an eye on things after launch. Small issues almost always surface in the first fortnight — a form going to the wrong inbox, a page nobody thought to check on a phone — and those are on us to fix.

If you spot anything at all, post it in the questions thread and we'll pick it up.

Keeping the site healthy

From here you have two options: look after the site yourself using the site management guide, or hand it to us.

Setup note: your care plan

Rewrite the care plan section above to match what you actually offer, and add your price. It's a synced pattern — edit it once and every portal using it updates, so your offer never goes stale in an old client's portal. Add a link to your checkout or booking page underneath. Delete this note before sharing.

⚡️ Quick tip

Put the care plan in front of the client at handover, not three months later when something breaks. The moment they're happiest with the work is the moment a maintenance plan reads as looking after something valuable rather than an upsell. Keeping it in the portal means the conversation happens without you having to start it.

synced_patterns.title: Care plan
synced_patterns.post_content:
Our care plan

A website isn't finished when it launches. Plugins update, things break quietly, and small changes pile up. Our care plan covers all of that so you don't have to think about it.

Every month we:

  • Apply WordPress, plugin, and theme updates, and check nothing broke afterwards
  • Take daily backups and keep them somewhere separate from your host
  • Watch uptime and security, and deal with problems before you notice them
  • Include an allowance of small content changes — send them over and we'll do them

Billed monthly, cancel whenever you like. If you'd rather handle it yourself, the site management guide in this portal covers everything you need.
